top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct idea from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes: it removes light-shift, Doppler and recoil perturbations while interrogating thousands of atoms in parallel, which took systematic uncertainty from the 10^-16 range to 10^-18. The result has been reproduced and cross-checked by independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE), the two-name allocation to Katori (concept and first demonstration) and Ye (accuracy frontier) is the cleanest available, and a citation narrowly scoped to the lattice and the 10^-18 regime does not depend on unrealised fundamental-physics payoffs. No award is clearly worse than a verified, well-attributed achievement.
